column2: The Early Bird Catches the Leak: Unveiling Timing Side Channels in LLM Serving Systems

column9: Black-box co-tenant TTFT timing detects KV-cache and semantic-cache hits; token-by-token search recovers system prompts and peer users' prompts; leaks seen in SGLang, GPTCache and online services. column10: Eviction is used to reset state, not as the leaked signal; no LRU-targeted eviction probing of victim entries. No KV compression/eviction-policy (H2O, SnapKV) leakage. No resource-exhaustion study.
column11: prefix-cache timing leak; semantic-cache leak; eviction as attack tool; defense (K-token sharing)

column2: I Know What You Asked: Prompt Leakage via KV-Cache Sharing in Multi-Tenant LLM Serving

column10: Leak signal is LPM scheduling order, not eviction itself; eviction is inferred only to time prompt switching. No compression-policy leakage, no attack that reads victim content from what was evicted, no resource-exhaustion goal.

column10: Improves search efficiency over existing oracles; abstract does not state the observed signal or any eviction use. No compression, no exhaustion.
